name: GSG on 42 Ω microstrip: bad SIG contact (2 Ω)

example.note: The Tx signal tip lands with 2 Ω. The TDR steps up by 2 Ω at the tip and stays up, so the line reads about 44.6 Ω instead of 42.7 Ω: a bad contact quietly shifts every impedance behind it. |S11| even improves by about 1.5 dB, because the line now looks closer to 50 Ω, so a better return loss is no proof of a good landing. S11 and S22 no longer agree.
example.author: TDR Painter
